dogecoin.text: @adagoose2016 @SHANERAVENSFAN @ozyau @ProTheDoge ...but why would they? Why would Robinhood (largest dogecoin wallet), a publicly traded company, nuke the price of dogecoin by selling their own users' coins (illegally)? It'd literally kill them. I'm not counting on altruism, I'm counting on self preservation.

@adagoose2016 @SHANERAVENSFAN @ozyau @ProTheDoge How exactly can "whales" coordinate for a rug pull on dogecoin? Sell all their coins at once? 1) they'd lose billions of dollars, 2) they'd accomplish nothing long-term, and 3) dogecoin would still exist and the price would bounce back in a relatively short period.

@adagoose2016 @ozyau @SHANERAVENSFAN @ProTheDoge Any coin that is solely dedicated to making a profit for the people that own it is the literal definition of a Ponzi scheme. Dogecoin has always been about fast, secure, low-volume transactions for tipping and e-commerce. The hype is a side effect of its success, not the cause.

@adagoose2016 @ozyau @SHANERAVENSFAN @ProTheDoge Sure, anyone can advocate for anything. But "burning" Dogecoin, even if achieved, would defeat the purpose. You can't have a deflating currency. You only "burn" a coin to make the USD dollar value of it go up and make $ profit. That's a ponzi scheme, not a legitimate utility.

@adagoose2016 @ozyau @SHANERAVENSFAN @ProTheDoge No. They don't. No "whale" can have any impact on the supply of Dogecoin (or Bitcoin, Litecoin, etc) whatsoever unless they literally send their *own* coins to a black hole address.

@adagoose2016 @SHANERAVENSFAN @ozyau @ProTheDoge Bitcoin (and other legitimate coins, such as Dogecoin) *cannot* be rug-pulled. It is literally physically impossible. There is no organization or person on the planet that can singlehandedly control the supply, demand, or velocity of the coin.
